comparison_title: Model Objective Alignment Audit: Binary Logistic vs Conditional Softmax Logit
scientific_interpretation: Variant B (Conditional Logit MLE) directly optimizes the categorical cross-entropy of selecting the race winner from the candidate set (Plackett-Luce Rank-1 likelihood). When fixed lambda=1.0 unscaled regularization is applied, it penalizes grouped race-level log-likelihood differently than candidate-level binary loss. When regularization is tuned via nested chronological validation (e.g. lambda in [0.05, 1.0]), Conditional Logit MLE achieves Log Loss 1.3526, matching Variant A (Binary Logistic + Softmax, Log Loss 1.3551). Therefore, neither objective is fundamentally empirically superior when regularization scaling is treated fairly; the choice is an architectural formulation decision and must remain strictly decoupled from practice-information validation.
